title: Open, vendor-neutral track deduplication, correlation and blue-force drone identification for drone-dense tactical air pictures below the fire-control tier (with cross-fabric provenance/catalog)
problem: Brigade-and-below air pictures now receive overlapping detections of the same small drones from c-UAS radars, RF/acoustic/EO-IR sensors, blue-force tracking, friendly drone telemetry and partner feeds, and no vendor-neutral layer merges them into single, identified (friend/unknown/hostile) tracks with explainable confidence and auditable provenance before the operator is overloaded or a friendly drone is engaged.

user.exact_role: Counter-UAS operator / air-defense battle-management operator sitting at FAAD C2 or Lattice C-UAS, and the ADAM/BAE-cell battle captain who has to decide whether a track on the COP is a friendly quadcopter or a hostile FPV; at higher echelons the JICO / Joint Track Data Coordinator who manually resolves dual designations and duplicate tracks
user.echelon: Company through division (tactical), plus fixed-site base-defense cells; JICO at JTF/corps
organization_examples: Army ADA battalions and SHORAD/C-sUAS batteries using FAAD C2
USAF base-defense counter-drone units (AFRL counter-drone lab)

current_workflow: 1. Each sensor or system (c-UAS radar, RF detector, acoustic array, EO/IR camera, BFT, friendly drone GCS, partner Link 16/CoT feed) publishes its own track with its own ID to TAK Server, FAAD C2 or Lattice.

2. Vendor-internal correlation runs inside FAAD C2 or Lattice for the sensors that vendor has integrated; anything bridged in via CoT gateways or data-link forwarders can re-appear as a second icon with a different ID.
3. A human (operator, liaison, or JICO/Joint Track Data Coordinator) recognises the dual track, decides which is real, and merges/deletes by hand or issues change data orders.

4. Friendly drone flights are deconflicted procedurally (airspace control measures, launch announced by voice/chat); the operator manually matches a detected track to a known friendly flight window and geometry.
5. Engagement or jamming decision is taken under time pressure, often after voice confirmation; in EW-denied conditions cooperative signals (Remote-ID-like beacons, telemetry) may be absent.
6. No cross-system record survives of which sensor produced the merged track, with what quality, or why it was labelled friend/hostile (no provenance/catalog at tactical echelon).
current_solution: IBCS/JTMC composite tracking at the fire-control tier (heavy, classified, sensor-set specific); FAAD C2 (Northrop-developed, correlates multiple track sources, has an Advanced Battle Manager with fratricide mitigation, UC2 messaging interface tested at Purple Guardian/Yuma) for Army SHORAD/C-sUAS; Anduril Lattice fusion now designated by JIATF-401 as the common tactical C-UAS C2 (Mar 2026); Navy SENSEI buying a standalone 'Data Fusion Correlator' via EMC2 OTA (RFI Feb-Mar 2026); manual JICO track management on Link 16; procedural airspace control for friendly drones; vendor-specific friend/foe labelling in c-UAS UIs; Mode 5 IFF transponders sized for drones being marketed (vendor claim).
failure: It fails at the seam between fused pictures: correlation logic is siloed inside each vendor stack and each program buys its own correlator (SENSEI is buying one separately in 2026), bridged tracks duplicate, and there is no standardized, secure, low-bandwidth friendly-drone identity feed that c-UAS C2 can consume, so identification collapses to human pattern-matching under time pressure; Ukraine reporting claims up to ~50% of downed Ukrainian drones were lost to own EW/air defence before identification systems were introduced, and a US MWI analysis states the inability to distinguish friendly drones raises fratricide risk. Nothing at the edge provides explainable confidence, lineage or a catalog of which track source to trust.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) The place where correlation lives is the C2 product itself, and the two C2 owners (Northrop's FAAD C2 for Army SHORAD, Anduril's Lattice as the JIATF-401 common C-UAS C2 and NGC2 data-layer lead) treat fusion as their moat and integrate sensors into their own entity model; a third-party correlator is therefore structurally an 'auditor' the platform owner did not ask for. (2) Labelled multi-sensor drone track data and real friendly-flight data live at CUI/Secret in exercise and base-defense environments; startups without a sponsor cannot obtain the data to tune or prove false-merge/false-split rates, and the ID half touches IFF/crypto policy (AIMS Mode 5 certification, NSA keying) that no small company can set. (3) Buyers are fragmented (Army ADA via CPE Missiles & Space / FAAD C2, JIATF-401, Navy SENSEI via EMC2 OTA, USAF counter-drone lab, USMC PM LAV) and each buys a correlator or ID feature inside its own integrated system, so no single customer has issued a requirement for a neutral cross-fabric track identity/provenance service. The DIU Blue Object cohort (Exia Labs, Dunedain, Kinnami, etc.) shows startups are circling blue-force data integration, but at the enterprise/theater level, not the 4-10 Hz tactical air track.
technical_wedge: A vendor-neutral 'track identity and provenance service' that sits beside (not inside) FAAD C2 / Lattice / TAK: ingests CoT, UC2/JADC2 messaging, sensor-native track feeds and friendly-drone telemetry (MAVLink/GCS exports, flight-plan hashes, Remote-ID-style beacons where present); performs track-to-track association with explainable confidence (covariance-aware gating, multi-hypothesis association tuned for slow, low-RCS, clutter-heavy small-UAS tracks); assigns stable cross-fabric IDs; cross-references tracks against declared friendly flights (time/geometry/intent) to produce a friend/unknown probability with reasons; records lineage and per-producer quality metrics; and publishes merged tracks plus a UDRA-style catalog back over CoT/TAK and to the host C2 via its API. Runs on an edge box in DDIL. The identity/intent broadcast piece is a low-bandwidth CoT/MAVLink extension, not a new radio - the startup must avoid becoming an IFF hardware or crypto vendor.

mvp.what: An edge software service plus TAK/TAKX plugin that (a) fuses duplicate small-UAS tracks from at least three heterogeneous sensor feeds into single tracks with confidence and lineage, (b) auto-matches tracks to declared friendly flights and flags mismatches, and (c) exposes a catalog/provenance view an operator or auditor can query after the event.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Bench and small-range demo using commercial c-UAS sensors (e.g., a low-cost radar or RF detector, an EO/IR camera with tracker, ADS-B/Remote ID receiver), ATAK-CIV positions and a few commercial drones flying scripted routes; report dedup rate, false-merge/false-split rate, end-to-end latency at 4-10 Hz, and blue-ID precision/recall under simulated loss of cooperative signals; replayable synthetic scenarios with 50-200 simultaneous tracks.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That an independent layer reduces duplicate icons and blue/unknown confusion measurably (e.g., >90% dedup with <2% false merges on the test set), holds latency under 250 ms at 10 Hz on edge compute, degrades gracefully in DDIL/EW (no cooperative signal), and produces provenance an evaluator trusts - without requiring the host C2 vendor's cooperation beyond published interfaces (CoT/TAK, UC2).

data_requirement.what: Recorded multi-sensor small-UAS detections (radar plots/tracks, RF detections, acoustic, EO/IR tracks) with ground-truth drone positions and friendly flight logs; later CUI/Secret exercise captures with real sensor mixes and Link 16/UC2 message logs.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Phase 1: yes, unclassified - self-generated range data with commercial sensors and drones, public anti-UAV datasets and academic multi-sensor UAV tracking datasets, ADS-B/Remote ID feeds, DHS/FAA test-range programmes, synthetic scenario generators. Phase 2: only via a government sponsor (JIATF-401 demo, xTech, DIU, AFRL counter-drone lab) and requires facility clearance/CUI handling; the non-US-person founder cannot be assumed to access CUI export-controlled or classified data - needs counsel and likely a US-person-only data enclave.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% US-citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control; the German founder becoming a US permanent resident helps, the Indonesian founder's stake and role must be structured with counsel. The JIATF-401 marketplace vetting explicitly includes export-control review. C-UAS track data and FAAD C2/Lattice interface specs are likely CUI/ITAR-controlled; a non-US-person founder generally cannot access ITAR technical data without licensing - plan a US-person engineering enclave and get export counsel before any sponsor data arrives. EMC2/OTA consortia are more flexible on foreign ownership than SBIR but still apply data-access rules. Not legal advice.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily for the correlation and blue-drone-feed functions: Anduril already owns the entity model and the JIATF-401 backbone and could ingest friendly-drone telemetry natively; Northrop can extend FAAD C2's correlator and ABM; Palantir can add it to Maven/NGC2 apps. The one piece incumbents are structurally less motivated to build is an independent, government-owned provenance/quality audit of their own fusion output.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if the government decides it wants a neutral, auditable correlation/identity service it controls (to avoid Lattice or FAAD C2 lock-in) and funds it as such - e.g., through the JIATF-401 CSO, the SENSEI-style standalone correlator buys, or an NGC2 'right to integrate' slot. Evidence that the government buys correlators separately (SENSEI 2026) and pays for blue-object integration (DIU 2025) supports this; the March 2026 Lattice designation cuts against it. Recommendation: pursue only as the neutral identity/provenance service with an explicit government-ownership pitch, or reject.

Production: hardening to host-C2 accreditation (ATO/RMF), sustainment, 24/7 support, plus the cost of a cleared US-person engineering team; assumes no IFF hardware or crypto development (which would multiply costs). regulatory_burden.explanation: The correlation software itself may be dual-use, but the moment it consumes military C-UAS sensor track formats, FAAD C2/Lattice interface specifications, or Link 16/IFF-related data it is likely ITAR technical data or CUI; exercise data is CUI/Secret; a fielded product needs an ATO under the host C2's accreditation; the JIATF-401 marketplace vetting includes export-control review; SBIR requires US ownership/control; and any IFF-adjacent identity function drifts toward AIMS/NSA policy. These are constraints to be scoped with counsel, not legal conclusions.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a US person generally cannot receive ITAR-controlled technical data or hold a US security clearance; a deemed-export licence is possible in principle but slow and uncertain for defense articles. Practical structure: keep the non-US founder on business/finance and unclassified commercial-product work behind an access-controlled enclave, plan for a FOCI mitigation review if the equity stake is material, and get export/FOCI counsel before the first CUI data or sponsor demo. The German founder's permanent residency (expected) resolves the US-person question for ITAR purposes but a clearance still requires citizenship in most cases. Not legal advice.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Airport, stadium, critical-infrastructure and prison counter-drone operators (DHS, FAA test sites, utilities, event security) face the same multi-sensor duplicate-track and 'is that our inspection drone?' problem, and UTM/Remote ID makes cooperative ID data available; but the civil market is crowded with integrated C-UAS vendors (Dedrone/Axon and others) with built-in fusion, budgets are smaller, and the US civil market is gated by counter-UAS authorities. Dual-use path is real but is a beachhead for data and validation rather than the revenue base.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility comes from (1) labelled multi-sensor small-UAS track data with ground truth accumulated across ranges and exercises (needed to tune association gates and blue-ID priors), (2) a library of validated integrations (CoT/TAK, UC2, sensor-native formats, GCS telemetry), (3) accreditation history inside a host C2 baseline, and (4) being the government's chosen neutral auditor. Algorithms alone are not defensible (well-known literature); provenance/catalog is unglamorous but sticky once units rely on it for after-action and engagement review.

why_now: Three things changed in 2023-2026: (1) friendly small-drone density exploded (Army accepted 12,080 Gauntlet 1 drones by Sept 2026 with drones-to-every-squad intent; Ukraine targeting millions of drones) while Ukraine documented severe drone fratricide and fielded UA DroneID; (2) the US consolidated C-sUAS under JIATF-401 (Aug 2025), opened a C-UAS marketplace (IOC Feb 2026), designated Lattice as common tactical C2 (Mar 2026) and launched an Army NGC2 common data layer (Jun 2026) - creating both the integration surface and the lock-in anxiety that a neutral layer answers; (3) the government is visibly buying correlation as a separate component (SENSEI Data Fusion Correlator RFI, Feb 2026) and paying startups for blue-object integration (DIU/INDOPACOM Dec 2025), plus policy mandates for data catalogs and UDRA-style provenance at tactical echelons.
killer_risk: Absorption plus policy pre-emption: the two functions this company would sell - track correlation and blue-drone identification - are core to the products of the vendors the government just designated as backbones (Lattice for JIATF-401 and NGC2; FAAD C2 for Army SHORAD), and the identity half may be settled by a mandated cooperative-ID/IFF or Remote-ID policy that any C2 simply consumes. A two-founder team with a non-US-person co-founder would spend 12-18 months on clearance, export and data-access plumbing before it could prove a false-merge rate on real data, by which time the feature likely ships inside Lattice or FAAD C2. Absence of a neutral layer today is not proof anyone will pay for one.

allied_extension: Yes, materially more compelling with allies, for three reasons: (1) Ukraine has the acute version of the problem (reported ~50% friendly-fire drone losses before ID systems; UA DroneID fielded), so the pain and test data exist there, though a US startup selling into Ukraine faces its own export and access issues; (2) NATO/European forces run mixed-vendor C-UAS stacks (SitaWare, national C2, SAPIENT-style open sensor interfaces in the UK, an EU JRC open-source C-UAS sensor-data-fusion group exists) where a vendor-neutral correlator is more natural than in a US market that just picked Lattice; (3) coalition track exchange at Bold Quest needed translation standards and produced duplicate/conflicting pictures, so cross-fabric provenance has a coalition buyer. Constraint: a German founder may find the German/European route (Helsing, Rheinmetall, Hensoldt ecosystems; EDF/EDA funding) easier than US ITAR-gated C-UAS work, but that is a different company from the US-first plan and dilutes focus.
